en: Udāna 7.10 Utenasutta Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Park.
Now at that time, while King Udena had gone to his pleasure garden, the royal palace had been burnt down, and five hundred women, headed by Sāmāvatī, had perished.
Then, in the morning, a number of bhikkhus dressed themselves, took their bowls and robes, and entered Kosambī for alms.

Having walked for alms in Kosambī, after their meal and returning from their almsround, those bhikkhus approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side.
As they were sitting there, those bhikkhus said this to the Blessed One:
"Venerable sir, while King Udena was in his pleasure grove, his inner palace was set on fire, and five hundred women, headed by Sāmāvatī, have died."
“Bhante, what is the destination, what is the future state of those female lay followers?
“There are, bhikkhus, among them female lay followers who are stream-enterers; there are those who are once-returners; there are those who are non-returners.
All those female lay followers, bhikkhus, have passed away without their attainment being fruitless.”
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
“The world is bound by delusion,
yet it appears as if it were capable [of liberation].”
The fool, bound by acquisitions and enveloped in darkness,
appears as if he were eternal.
For one who sees thus, there is nothing whatsoever.
The tenth.
Its summary:
Dve Bhaddiya and Dve Satta,
Lakuṇḍaka Taṇhākkhaya,
and Kaccāna Papañcakhaya.
"And the well, and the water.
This is the seventh chapter, the Cūḷavagga.
